author: bshastry
content:
I am working on another edge case. ELs validate structural integrity of BAL within a signed envelope. So a hostile builder can outbid and then declare a BAL in the signed envelope reveal with a claim that tx0 in the block changes code at common empty target T (no code at this addr) from zero to some large value (under 64KB). Because subsequent txs call the same target (albeit no calldata), the BAL validator in the ELs does the work of actually executing tx1...txN in parallel against this pre state of T holding that code. This involves hashing, sometimes jumpdest analysis etc.

Because the txs are otherwise cheap (intrinsic gas may be sufficient), you can pack 10k of them within SSZ envelope of 10Mb, and make ELs do the expensive work (16 cores ethrex takes 22s walltime on such an adversarial BAL).  Eventually, the attacker only pays bid fee since block is invalid, so it is a relatively cheap primitive to exercise
